person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: generic object detection with deep learning - what the problem is, how it is scored, and what more than 300 papers have done to it
span.quote: The goal of object detection is to determine whether there are any instances of objects from given categories (such as humans, cars, bicycles, dogs or cats) in an image and, if present, to return the spatial location and extent of each object instance

span.label: what the field has achieved since deep learning arrived, organised by detection framework, feature representation, proposal generation, context modelling, training strategy and evaluation metric
span.quote: More than 300 research contributions are included in this survey, covering many aspects of generic object detection: detection frameworks, object feature representation, object proposal generation, context modeling, training strategies, and evaluation metrics. We finish the survey by identifying promising directions for future research.

span.label: a survey of more than 300 contributions with an explicit account of how detection is evaluated - including that a detection counts as correct only above a chosen overlap threshold, and that the threshold changed
span.quote: More than 300 research contributions are included in this survey, covering many aspects of generic object detection: detection frameworks, object feature representation, object proposal generation, context modeling, training strategies, and evaluation metrics. We finish the survey by identifying promising directions for future research.

span.label: critique
span.quote: In practice, current detectors focus mainly on structured object categories, such as the 20, 200 and 91 object classes in PASCAL VOC (Everingham et al. 2010), ILSVRC (Russakovsky et al. 2015) and MS COCO (Lin et al. 2014) respectively. Clearly, the number of object categories under consideration in existing benchmark datasets is much smaller than can be recognized by humans.

span.label: a field whose measure of success is a threshold and whose object vocabulary is a benchmark's class list - 20, 200 or 91 depending which benchmark
span.quote: In practice, current detectors focus mainly on structured object categories, such as the 20, 200 and 91 object classes in PASCAL VOC (Everingham et al. 2010), ILSVRC (Russakovsky et al. 2015) and MS COCO (Lin et al. 2014) respectively. span.label: a structured literature survey organised by component of the detection pipeline, with a table reconciling the evaluation metrics used by PASCAL VOC, ILSVRC, MS COCO and Open Images

span.label: a detection counts as a true positive when its category matches AND its overlap with the ground-truth box is not smaller than a predefined threshold. Every precision, recall and AP number in the field is downstream of that number - and the number is a convention, not a derivation
span.quote: A predicted detection (b, c, p) is regarded as a True Positive (TP) if • The predicted category c equals the ground truth label cg. • The overlap ratio IOU (Intersection Over Union) (Everingham et al. 2010; Russakovsky et al. 2015) IOU(b, bg) = area (b ∩ bg) area (b ∪ bg) , (4) between the predicted BB b and the ground truth bg is not smaller than a predefined threshold

span.label: PASCAL VOC's mAP is computed at a single IoU of 0.5; MS COCO's is averaged across 0.5 to 0.95 in steps of 0.05. Both are called mAP. A survey of the field has to print a table of which benchmark means which, and any comparison across that boundary is comparing two definitions
span.term: the same metric name, two quantities
span.quote: Since the introduction of MS COCO, more attention has been placed on the accuracy of the bounding box location. Instead of using a fixed IOU threshold, MS COCO introduces a few metrics (summarized in Table 5) for characterizing the performance of an object detector. For instance, in contrast to the traditional mAP computed at a single IoU of 0.5, A Pcoco is averaged across all object categories and multiple IOU values from 0.5 to 0.95 in steps of 0.05.

span.label: 41% of MS COCO objects are small and 24% are large, so size-stratified metrics were introduced. THE AGGREGATE WAS MISLEADING BECAUSE OF WHAT THE DATASET CONTAINED, and the response was to change the measure rather than the data
span.term: a metric subdivided because the dataset was skewed
span.quote: Because 41% of the objects in MS COCO are small and 24% are large, metrics A P small coco are also introduced.

span.label: 20 classes in PASCAL VOC, 200 in ILSVRC, 91 in MS COCO. `Object detection` means detection of whichever of those lists the paper trained against, and the survey says plainly that all of them are much smaller than what a human recognises

span.quote: In practice, current detectors focus mainly on structured object categories, such as the 20, 200 and 91 object classes in PASCAL VOC (Everingham et al. 2010), ILSVRC (Russakovsky et al. 2015) and MS COCO (Lin et al. 2014) respectively. Clearly, the number of object categories under consideration in existing benchmark datasets is much smaller than can be recognized by humans.

span.label: one figure panel shows a single class spanning wildly different images; another shows four near-identical images from four different classes. So a detector cannot be evaluated on visual similarity, and the annotation is the only ground truth there is

span.quote: Changes in appearance of the same class with variations in imaging conditions (a–h). There is an astonishing variation in what is meant to be a single object class (i). In contrast, the four images in j appear very similar, but in fact are from four different object classes.

span.label: THE LONGEST TERM LIST IN THE CORPUS, AND IT IS NOT A LIST OF SYNONYMS - IT IS A LIST OF TERMS WHOSE BOUNDARIES DISAGREE BETWEEN PAPERS, AND IT SITS IN A FOOTNOTE: `To the best of our knowledge, THERE IS NO UNIVERSAL AGREEMENT IN THE LITERATURE ON THE DEFINITIONS OF VARIOUS VISION SUBTASKS. Terms such as detection, localization, recognition, classification, categorization, verification, identification, annotation, labeling, and understanding ARE OFTEN DIFFERENTLY DEFINED (Andreopoulos and Tsotsos 2013)`. Ten terms, attributed, declared unagreed, in a footnote - and the survey then has to pick.
span.quote: To the best of our knowledge, there is no universal agreement in the literature on the definitions of various vision subtasks. Terms such as detection, localization, recognition, classification, categorization, verification, identification, annotation, labeling, and understanding are often differently defined (Andreopoulos and Tsotsos 2013)

span.label: whether a detection is correct depends on a predefined overlap threshold rather than on any property of the image
span.quote: A predicted detection (b, c, p) is regarded as a True Positive (TP) if • The predicted category c equals the ground truth label cg. • The overlap ratio IOU (Intersection Over Union) (Everingham et al. 2010; Russakovsky et al. 2015) IOU(b, bg) = area (b ∩ bg) area (b ∪ bg) , (4) between the predicted BB b and the ground truth bg is not smaller than a predefined threshold

span.label: mAP means different things under PASCAL VOC and MS COCO, so numbers are not comparable across that boundary
span.quote: Since the introduction of MS COCO, more attention has been placed on the accuracy of the bounding box location. Instead of using a fixed IOU threshold, MS COCO introduces a few metrics (summarized in Table 5) for characterizing the performance of an object detector. For instance, in contrast to the traditional mAP computed at a single IoU of 0.5, A Pcoco is averaged across all object categories and multiple IOU values from 0.5 to 0.95 in steps of 0.05.

span.label: the number of object categories in existing benchmark datasets is much smaller than can be recognized by humans - 20, 200 and 91 against a real-world order of 10^4-10^5
span.quote: In practice, current detectors focus mainly on structured object categories, such as the 20, 200 and 91 object classes in PASCAL VOC (Everingham et al. 2010), ILSVRC (Russakovsky et al. 2015) and MS COCO (Lin et al. 2014) respectively. Clearly, the number of object categories under consideration in existing benchmark datasets is much smaller than can be recognized by humans.

span.label: the challenge winner is decided by the number of object categories won, with mAP used as a team measure justified by the two rankings having always agreed
span.quote: In object detection challenges, such as PASCAL VOC and ILSVRC, the winning entry of each object category is that with the highest AP score, and the winner of the challenge is the team that wins on the most object categories. The mAP is also used as the measure of a team’s Footnote 3 continued performance, and is justified since the ranking of teams by mAP was always the same as the ranking by the number of object categories won (Russakovsky et al. 2015).

span.label: high accuracy and high efficiency are competing goals, so any single reported figure is a position on a trade-off rather than a level of performance
span.quote: The ideal of generic object detection is to develop a generalpurpose algorithm that achieves two competing goals of high quality/accuracy and high efficiency (Fig. 5). As illustrated in Fig. 6, high quality detection must accurately localize and recognize objects in images or video frames, such that the large variety of object categories in the real world can be distinguished (i.e., high distinctiveness), and that object instances from the same category, subject to intraclass appearance variations, can be localized and recognized (i.e., high robustness). High efficiency requires that the entire detection task runs in real time with acceptable memory and storage demands.

span.label: precision and recall from information retrieval, carried into vision as the basis of average precision and then of the field's single headline number
span.quote: The most commonly used metric is Average Precision (AP), derived from precision and recall. AP is usually evaluated in a category specific manner, i.e., computed for each object category separately. To compare performance over all object categories, the mean AP (mAP) averaged over all object categories is adopted as the final measure of performance

span.label: MS COCO's average over ten IoU thresholds instead of a single 0.5
